string.ub__tax_document_forms_details_content_m:
"Uber may issue three kinds of 1099 tax forms - 1099-K, 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC to partners meeting certain criteria. 
 
For most states 1099-K tax forms are issued only to partners who earned more than $20,000 and generated 200 or more transactions (trips, deliveries) during the year. However, the minimum income threshold for a 1099-K is $600 in Massachusetts, Vermont, Washington D.C., Virginia, Maryland and California; $1,000 in New Jersey, Illinois; and $1,200 in Missouri. 
 
For Puerto Rico the minimum income threshold for a 480.6SP tax form is $500. 
 
Your state residency is established based on your address in Tax Settings. If you haven’t provided an address there, then your residency will be established based on the address you provided when you registered on the platform. 
 
1099-MISC tax forms are issued only to partners who received at least $600 in miscellaneous payments (referrals, incentives and other payments not derived from trips or deliveries) during the tax year. 
 
If you earned less than $600 in such miscellaneous payments during the year, Uber would not issue a 1099-MISC. 
 
1099-MISC tax forms may be issued to partners residing in all 50 states in the U.S., if they earned at least $600. Starting in the 2020 tax year, Uber will also issue 1099-NEC tax forms to partners in all US states with earnings over $600."

"Your 1099-K is an official IRS tax document that reports your annual on-trip gross earnings. Gross earnings are the total amount paid by riders and Uber Eats users for the rides and/or deliveries you completed. 
You’ll get a 1099-K if you have $5,000 or more in gross trip/order earnings. For more details, visit the IRS website. 
 
Note: some states have lower thresholds, so you might get a 1099-K for earning less than $5,000. If you had backup withholding during the year, you’ll get a 1099-K no matter how much you earned. Backup withholding will be shown in Box 4 of the form. 
 
1099 NEC is an official IRS tax document reports promotions, referrals, and other miscellaneous payments for the year. Only drivers and delivery people who received $600 or more of these types of payments will receive a 1099-NEC. For more details, visit IRS.gov."

"If you didn't meet IRS or
 state reporting thresholds, Uber isn't required to issue a 1099-K. You can opt in to receive one.

If you opt in before 31 Dec, you'll receive your form by 31 Jan.
If you opt in after 31 Dec , you'll receive it within one month of opting in.

Your 1099-K is an official IRS tax document that reports your annual on-trip gross earnings. Gross earnings are the total amount paid by riders and Uber Eats users for the rides and/or deliveries you completed.
You'll get a 1099-K if you have $20,000 or more in gross trip/order earnings. For more details, visit the [IRS website](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/understanding-your-form-1099-k).

Note: some states have lower thresholds, so you might get a 1099-K for earning less than $20,000. If you had backup withholding during the year, you'll get a 1099-K no matter how much you earned. Backup withholding will be shown in Box 4 of the form.

1099 NEC is an official IRS tax document that reports promotions, referrals, and other miscellaneous payments for the year. Only driver-partners and delivery people who received $600 or more of these types of payments will receive a 1099-NEC. For more details, visit [IRS.gov](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-1099-nec)"

string.ub_tax_document_summary_details:
"To help you keep track of your business activity on the platform, Uber provides an outline of your earnings and business-related expenses. 

You can download and share your tax summaries right here on your phone as PDF files, or on a desktop computer via the Tax Information page on the Partner Portal at https://drivers.uber.com/ 

We suggest that you seek tax guidance from a qualified tax professional."
string.ub_tax_document_summary_details_v2:
"The Uber tax summary gives a breakdown of your monthly and annual earnings and business expenses that might be tax-deductible. What you can deduct depends on how your business is set up. 
 
The tax summary will also include all your online miles, which may be deductible. These miles include miles driven waiting for a trip/order, driving to pick up a rider/order, and driving to the drop-off location.
 
You can download your tax summaries here in the Driver app or from your web driver dashboard.
We recommend that you seek advice from a tax service like TurboTax or a tax professional to understand your possible deductions."
